entries.reason: Transform applied (exact single match; result equals the proposer's resultingText). Every other part passes. Placement ('straight after the owner word', children's, boys') is correct and serves ENG-003-A-PU-05. No clause is false on any of the 4 carriers, and the its/it's swap is conditional. Sentences of 4, 15, 9 and 8 words end on full stops, British English. REFUSE, and the fault is in the sentence I suggested, not the proposer's application of it. 'The owner words its, his, hers and theirs never have one.' reads as a COMPLETE list of exceptions to 'An owner needs an apostrophe'. So it still implies that ours, yours and whose need one, and that teaches our's and your's, the same error class I refused in G2. My G2 note said I would attest with that change; on re-checking, my list was incomplete, and I would rather say so than attest a sentence I now know over-claims. Fix that makes the list openly non-exhaustive: change 'The owner words its, his, hers and theirs never have one.' to 'Owner words like its, his, ours and theirs never have one.' That is 9 words, true as grammar, and 'like' stops it being read as the whole list. With that change and nothing else, I would attest.
